newsitem.title: USA: U.S. farmers say EPA clean air study flawed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. farmers say EPA clean air study flawed.

text.p: U.S. agriculture will be hurt by the Environmental Protection Agency's proposed new clean air standards to limit particulate matter, the American Farm Bureau Federation told a Senate panel on Tuesday.

An emissions inventory used by the EPA is flawed, and inaccurately estimated the number of times that a farmer drives his tractor over a field, said California Farm Bureau president Bob Vice. He testified before the Senate Environment and Public Works subcommittee on clean air.

"But probably the most blatant example, which would have cost the agricultural industry thousands of dollars, was the initial emission inventory for combusion engines used to operate irrigation pumps," Vice said.

The EPA inventory estimated emissions of nitrogen oxide at 626 tons per day from all the irrigation pumps in the San Joaquin Valley, far exceeding cars and trucks which emit about 353 tons per day. But after farmers complained, another study was commissioned and found that the emission rate for the pumps was only 32 tons per day.
